title: Rosalind and the Smile
premise: Silas Winterbourne takes a teaching post at Hollowmere School, where a class of children vanished decades ago and the town insists they simply moved away. When Silas inherits their grandmother Rosalind's house, the old photographs begin showing an extra chair at every table—a chair that moves closer with each passing night. Silas learns that Rosalind survived the original disappearance by inviting something in and binding it to a bargain, one that now passes to her heir. To end it, Silas must un-invite what was welcomed in before sunrise on the anniversary night, knowing the entity will demand a replacement: either Silas or someone Silas loves.
about_author: Emrys Marchetti is the pen name of a former rural schoolteacher who spent years collecting local disappearance legends before turning them into fiction. They write horror that treats inheritance—of houses, debts, and bargains—as the truest kind of haunting.

chapters.title: The Empty Desks
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Arriving in Hollowmere, Silas is assigned Room 4, where thirteen desks sit unused and no one will say why. The headmaster's smile doesn't reach his eyes. Emotional beat: uneasy curiosity; Silas's rationalism established as armor against a wrongness they refuse to name.

chapters.title: Grandmother's House
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Silas moves into Rosalind Winterbourne's inherited cottage, finding salt lines at every threshold and a journal locked in a drawer. A neighbor warns them to keep the curtains drawn after dark. Emotional beat: grief tangled with dread; the house feels less like a gift than a duty.

chapters.title: An Extra Chair
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Sorting photographs for the funeral reception, Silas notices a wooden chair in images from 1974 onward—a chair no one remembers owning, always one seat closer to the camera each decade. Emotional beat: denial cracking; the first undeniable evidence that something has been waiting.

chapters.title: What the Children Left Behind
chapters.summary: POV alternating Silas and retired teacher Mabel Crowe. Mabel recounts the night Room 4 emptied mid-lesson and how Rosalind was the only adult present who came home whole. Emotional beat: horrified recognition; Silas realizes their grandmother was the survivor, not the innocent.

chapters.title: The Journal of Rosalind Winterbourne
chapters.summary: POV Silas, interleaved with Rosalind's journal entries. The entries reveal the bargain: invited in to spare the town, the thing took the children instead, and Rosalind paid yearly to keep it fed elsewhere. Emotional beat: betrayal and pity intertwined; inheritance revealed as a debt.

chapters.title: Closer Every Night
chapters.summary: POV Silas. The chair appears in the cottage itself now, real wood under Silas's hand, warm as a body. Each dawn it sits nearer to Silas's bed. The headmaster quietly cancels school for the anniversary week. Emotional beat: claustrophobic escalation; time becomes the antagonist.

chapters.title: The Terms of Survival
chapters.summary: POV Silas and Mabel. Deciphering the final journal pages, they learn the entity can be un-invited only by its host, spoken aloud before sunrise—but whoever speaks must offer a life in exchange, and the thing prefers willing ones. Emotional beat: grim resolve; Silas begins planning a sacrifice they haven't admitted aloud.

chapters.title: Anniversary
chapters.summary: POV Silas. On the night, the town seals its doors while the cottage fills with the smell of chalk dust and cold breath. The missing children appear at the windows, unchanged since 1974, mouthing warnings. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into tenderness; the victims are not the threat but the proof.

chapters.title: Un-Invited
chapters.summary: POV Silas. At the threshold, Silas speaks the revocation—and offers themselves—but the entity reveals the loophole Rosalind used: a willing substitute may stand proxy. Silas instead names the truth of the bargain aloud, breaking its power over consent. Climax: the chair splinters; the house exhales; dawn breaks through broken curtains.

chapters.title: Room 4, Reopened
chapters.summary: POV Silas, months later. Thirteen desks fill with living students; the photographs show empty rooms at last. Silas keeps the splintered chair leg on their desk as a reminder that survival always costs, and someone must choose to pay honestly. Emotional beat: hard-won peace; the price of survival acknowledged rather than forgotten.
